title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #114 review (scripts-validate-tasks-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #114 (scripts-validate-tasks-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/tasks/done/scripts-validate-tasks-followups.json's second `decisions` entry (recorded_by task-worker, covering the index_by_id list-keying fix, the shebang drop, and the is_invalid_str_choice helper) carries `timestamp: "2026-09-18T00:00:00Z"` -- an exact-midnight value that looks like a placeholder rather than the real time the decision was made. The corresponding commit (f16ff55, 'Fix validate_tasks.py's index.json duplicate-id overwrite bug') was actually authored at 2026-09-18T12:27:07Z per `git log`, ~12.5 hours off from the recorded timestamp. `scripts/validate_tasks.py`'s own validator only checks that `decisions[].timestamp` is a non-empty string, not that it's plausible/real, so this slipped through undetected. Not blocking (doesn't affect the decision's actual content or the code it describes), but worth correcting the timestamp to the real commit time (or removing it if the exact real time can't be reconstructed) so the decision record doesn't misrepresent when the call was made -- and worth a reminder that a fabricated/rounded timestamp on a `decisions` entry is the same class of problem CLAUDE.md/pr-merger already guard against for `review.reviewed_at`.

decisions.decision: Corrected docs/tasks/done/scripts-validate-tasks-followups.json's second `decisions` entry timestamp from the fabricated/rounded "2026-09-18T00:00:00Z" to "2026-09-18T12:27:07Z", the exact author/committer date of commit f16ff55 ('Fix validate_tasks.py's index.json duplicate-id overwrite bug'), which is the commit that made the decision that entry documents (the index_by_id list-keying fix, the shebang drop, and the is_invalid_str_choice helper).
decisions.rationale: `git log --format="%H %aI %cI %s" f16ff55` shows both author and committer date as 2026-09-18T12:27:07Z, an unambiguous single timestamp for when that specific commit landed, matching the checklist item's own citation of that commit and timestamp. No other candidate commit touches those three fixes, so there's no reconstruction ambiguity here.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered removing the timestamp field entirely per the checklist item's fallback option ('or removing it if the exact real time can't be reconstructed'); rejected since the exact real time *could* be reconstructed unambiguously via git log, so correcting it is strictly more useful than removing it.

review.notes: Trivial scope: corrects a fabricated/rounded decisions[].timestamp in docs/tasks/done/scripts-validate-tasks-followups.json to commit f16ff55's real author/committer date. Independently re-verified via `git log --format="%H %aI %cI %s" f16ff55` -- both author and committer date are 2026-09-18T12:27:07Z, matching the PR's corrected value exactly. `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` passes clean (124 task files, no violations); `python3 scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py` passes 24/24. Diff touches only 3 task-board JSON files (no application code), so backend/frontend tests, coverage, static analysis, code-review skill, elder-signal/architecture review, OpenAPI regeneration, and browser walkthrough/e2e suite are all inapplicable -- explicitly noted rather than silently skipped. Checklist item is done and backed by a proper decisions entry (decision + rationale + alternatives_considered). No pr_decision present to clear. No findings, nothing to track as a new follow-up.
